utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-00-41-PT, the Prosecutor versus Pasko Ljubicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good afternoon, Mr. Ljubicic. Can you hear me in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can understand everything you say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a problem. I am not receiving any interpretation. I can't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I repeat?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, of course. Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can hear you, and I can fully understand what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Please sit down. I'd like to ask for the appearances for the sake of the transcript. The Prosecution first of all, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Mr. Jonjic. My name is Mark Harmon, appearing on behalf of the Prosecutor. Appearing with me today, to my right, is Mr. Fergal Gaynor, and to my left, Ms. Kamala Janakiram, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And could the Defence counsel please present itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Tomislav Jonjic on behalf of Mr. Pasko Ljubicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Jonjic. I would like to remind you that pursuant to the scheduling order dated the 13th of May, 2003, this hearing will be concerned with -- will be a Status Conference pursuant to Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The purpose is to discuss the progress achieved in preparing for the case. And I think that we are now approaching the end of the pre-trial phase, and the scheduling order contains some dates. The Prosecution has to file its pre-trial brief and its list of witnesses on the 10th of June, 2003, and the Defence should file its pre-trial brief on the 7th of July, 2003. Are there any comments that the parties would like to make with regard to this matter? Does the Prosecution find that these dates are appropriate, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We are well underway, and we will meet that trial date -- that date for filing the pre-trial brief. We're satisfied with those dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. And Mr. Jonjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the same is true of the Defence. We shall meet the deadline set by the Court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Jonjic. I would now like to ask Madam Registrar for us to move into private session. And please tell me when we are ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Do any of the parties -- does one of the parties have some issues they would like to raise? Before I give Mr. Ljubicic the chance to take the floor, Mr. Harmon, do you have anything you would like to comment on?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We have nothing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And Mr. Jonjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence, now that we have been given the opportunity, would like to seize this opportunity to talk about two or three minor details concerning the preparation of our Defence. The Prosecution is still disclosing evidence. We don't know how far they still are from the end of this process. However, we do deem it necessary to inform the Court that Bosnia and Herzegovina in part acted on the request by the Court dated 3rd of February this year, and the Defence have received part of the documents required by the Court in its decision. On the other hand, the Defence deems it necessary to announce that it may address with a similar request the Republic of Croatia concerning binding orders for documents to be handed over. The Defence has made many requests to the Republic of Croatia to disclose documents, and only part of it has been met with so far. The Defence will shortly decide whether time is ripe to file a similar request with the Court concerning the Republic of Croatia this time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Jonjic. But if I've understood you correctly, you asked whether the Prosecution had accomplished its obligation of disclosing exhibits, or did I fail to understand what you said? Because you dealt with two issues; firstly you spoke about the documents from the Prosecution, and then you spoke about documents that might be located in one country or another country. With regard to the Prosecution, are you asking -- are you making a formal request? Have they, in your opinion, fulfilled their obligation of transmitting all the exhibits to you, even those of an exculpatory nature?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Prosecution has given over to the Defence most, we believe, of the statements, but we don't know if the process has been completed, the process of disclosure, or whether they have more to disclose before the pre-trial briefs. We don't know if this process has been completed or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Harmon, what is your position on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We are in the process of continuing to disclose information that is relevant and applicable under the Rules. We have disclosed the bulk of the material that we're required to under the Rules. I know there is yet another production that consists of some additional statements, not many, consist of some additional exhibits, not many, some audiotapes, again not many, so we will produce those. We have an arrangement with Mr. Jonjic in terms of delivery of those. We have a satisfactory arrangement. We will contact Mr. Jonjic about how he wants those delivered and where, and we will abide by the normal practice that we have between the parties. That's what I can say at this point in time. I will add, of course, that investigation continues to be ongoing, and as we continue to get additional information, we will turn it over very quickly to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no doubt that you will cooperate to the best of your ability. And I think that all pending issues, all pending matters, can be transmitted to our honourable colleague Mr. Harhoff who, as always, is available to assist in this case. Mr. Ljubicic, I would like to ask you about your health. Do you have complaints of any kind? Would you like to inform me of anything that might be inconvenient or any possible problems?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no objections to make concerning my sojourn in the Detention Unit. The way the personnel have been treating me is completely fair. My health is very good. The only thing that remains for me to do now is to wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I think that there is nothing else to deal with with regard to this issue. Yet again, I would like to invite the parties to contact Mr. Harhoff for any matters that need to be resolved, and I'm sure that he will not fail to attempt to resolve any problems that may arise. And I think that we can now adjourn. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: at 2.40 p.m.
